Note: HTTP egress is permanently out of scope (docs/scope.md §3.2). This test declares no TestHttpRequestPolicy and performs a real outbound GET; on real BC that is allowed and the test passes, which is the evidence the runner adopts for treating an absent policy as AllowAllOutboundRequests. BC's own dispatcher therefore hands the request on to be sent for real, and it is refused at the runner's egress boundary. Since #2547 the throw site is the Cecil-rewritten NavHttpClient.SendAsync(DataError, HttpRequestMessage, ByRef) — the one method every real send funnels through — rather than the AL verbs, which must run for BC's [HttpClientHandler] dispatcher to be reached at all. It raises a BC-native NavNCLDialogException carrying the documented 'out-of-scope: HttpClient.Get — external-http — see docs/scope.md#external-http' message (the verb is read back off the request's HTTP method, so the refusal still names the API the AL author touched): measured, a plain CLR exception thrown from that frame is replaced by BC with a generic NavNCLInvalidOperationException and the out-of-scope signal is lost. Since #1743 expect-oos recognises both the typed exception and the message convention.
